air:machine-readable-format.scope_note: Indicator A1 of the AI-ready data framework. Product available as structured data (CSV/JSON/parquet), not PDF-only

air:programmatic-access.scope_note: Indicator A2 of the AI-ready data framework. Documented public API; auth model; rate limits stated

air:bulk-access.scope_note: Indicator A3 of the AI-ready data framework. Full-product bulk download exists and is linked from product page

air:crawler-agent-access.scope_note: Indicator A4 of the AI-ready data framework. robots.txt + AI-crawler policy permit retrieval; no soft-blocks on data paths

air:discoverability-surface.scope_note: Indicator A5 of the AI-ready data framework. llms.txt (or equivalent) present; sitemap covers data products

air:structured-markup.scope_note: Indicator A6 of the AI-ready data framework. schema.org/Dataset (or DCAT/Croissant) markup valid on product pages

air:stable-identifier.scope_note: Indicator A7 of the AI-ready data framework. Persistent URLs/DOIs for products and vintages

air:timeliness-of-surface.scope_note: Indicator A8 of the AI-ready data framework. Release date machine-readable; latest-vintage pointer resolvable

air:m2m-agent-surface.scope_note: Indicator A9 of the AI-ready data framework. Product exposes a machine-first entry point (documented API plus MCP/A2A-class endpoint or equivalent agent protocol); human pages derivable from it

air:application-data-tool-machine-surfac.scope_note: Indicator A10 of the AI-ready data framework. Interactive data tools expose stable, directly-requestable deep links; meaningful states are not fragment-only or session-dependent; invalid routes return true 404/410, not HTTP-200 shell (soft-404); page-specific content present in raw HTML before JS execution

air:effective-crawler-access.scope_note: Indicator A11 of the AI-ready data framework. A4 upgraded from declared-policy check to three-layer comparison: declared (robots.txt/meta directives) vs enforced (edge/WAF/bot-management treatment) vs observed (actual crawler request logs). A mismatch between layers is itself the finding, not an error state

air:variable-level-semantic.scope_note: Indicator B1 of the AI-ready data framework. Comprehensive variable-level metadata (labels, definitions, units, universes)

air:definition-surface.scope_note: Indicator B2 of the AI-ready data framework. Concept/term definitions published, versioned, linked from variables

air:methodology-legibility.scope_note: Indicator B3 of the AI-ready data framework. Methodology docs in structured text (not PDF-only); summarizable by retrieval

air:quality-metadata.scope_note: Indicator B4 of the AI-ready data framework. Data-quality attributes (error measures, suppression rules, revisions policy) published as metadata, not prose

air:semantic-consistency.scope_note: Indicator B5 of the AI-ready data framework. Same concept ⇒ same identifier across products/vintages

air:nl-affordance.scope_note: Indicator B6 of the AI-ready data framework. Plain-language product summary present and current (the retrieval target)

air:retrieval-grounded-qa-accuracy.scope_note: Indicator C1 of the AI-ready data framework. Benchmark question set per product; answer accuracy of a retrieval-paired model vs published values

air:faithfulness-of-ai-restatement.scope_note: Indicator C2 of the AI-ready data framework. Entailment-judged: do model statements about the product entail from product text? (probe protocol, re-aimed)

air:value-drift-resistance.scope_note: Indicator C3 of the AI-ready data framework. Version/vintage disambiguation: does retrieval return the vintage asked for?

air:citation-quality.scope_note: Indicator C4 of the AI-ready data framework. Generative engines citing the product cite the authoritative page (not aggregators)

air:readiness-metric-baseline.scope_note: Indicator C5 of the AI-ready data framework. Product scored against published AI-data-readiness metrics

air:license-clarity.scope_note: Indicator D1 of the AI-ready data framework. Explicit machine-readable license/terms on product and API

air:reuse-permission-for-ai.scope_note: Indicator D2 of the AI-ready data framework. Terms address model training/retrieval use explicitly

air:provenance-completeness.scope_note: Indicator D3 of the AI-ready data framework. Source lineage published (collection → processing → product)

air:no-dark-data.scope_note: Indicator D4 of the AI-ready data framework. Statutory products enumerable from a public inventory (data.gov/agency inventory current)

air:verification-vs-validation-split.scope_note: Indicator E1 of the AI-ready data framework. Product spec conformance (AUTO/DOC set) reported separately from fit-for-use evals (EVAL set); a product cannot pass validation while failing verification

air:acceptance-threshold.scope_note: Indicator E2 of the AI-ready data framework. Published pass/fail thresholds per eval, pre-registered before results; threshold changes are versioned events

air:instrument-versioning.scope_note: Indicator E3 of the AI-ready data framework. Eval sets and rubrics carry versions; results never pooled across versions

air:contamination-policy.scope_note: Indicator E4 of the AI-ready data framework. Public eval sets have a held-out rotation; publication schedule assumes training-set leakage within one model generation

air:positive-control.scope_note: Indicator E5 of the AI-ready data framework. Seeded known-bad items (canaries/decoys) in every continuous-eval cycle; a cycle with zero fired controls is INVALID, not passing

air:failure-attribution.scope_note: Indicator E6 of the AI-ready data framework. Discrepancy taxonomy localizing failures to retrieval / vintage / metadata / model; each stage instrumented

air:corrective-action-closure.scope_note: Indicator E7 of the AI-ready data framework. Documented path from failed eval back into the data product (metadata fix, vintage pointer, dictionary entry) with re-test; mean-time-to-closure tracked

air:drift-sentinel.scope_note: Indicator E8 of the AI-ready data framework. Versioned golden question/answer sets re-run on schedule against the product surface; baseline deltas alarmed; state fidelity across product versions measured, not assumed

air:adversarial-evaluation.scope_note: Indicator E9 of the AI-ready data framework. Standing adversarial bank: vintage traps, confusable series, unit traps, DP-noise misreads, suppression probes; plus surface red team — misparse and injection resistance of pages/markup/llms.txt. Reported as break modes, not just pass rates

air:pre-release-gate.scope_note: Indicator F1 of the AI-ready data framework. New releases pass a published expectation suite (schema validity, row/total sanity, identifier persistence) before going live

air:contract-stability.scope_note: Indicator F2 of the AI-ready data framework. API/schema changes are versioned; breaking changes announced with deprecation windows; compatibility checked mechanically

air:regression-on-vintage-transition.scope_note: Indicator F3 of the AI-ready data framework. Time-series identifiers, geography codes, and endpoints survive a new vintage or a crosswalk is published; tested per release

air:change-legibility.scope_note: Indicator F4 of the AI-ready data framework. Machine-readable changelog per release (what changed, why, revision class); webhooks/push for high-frequency products

air:staged-rollout.scope_note: Indicator F5 of the AI-ready data framework. Canary/staging surface for major product changes; AI-consumer regression run before promotion

air:release-authenticity.scope_note: Indicator F6 of the AI-ready data framework. Signed releases / provenance attestations so downstream copies are traceable to the authoritative artifact (SLSA-class, adapted)

air:uncertainty-legibility.scope_note: Indicator G1 of the AI-ready data framework. **G1-D (declared)** — error measures (MOEs, CVs, DP noise parameters) present as structured fields beside the estimates on the product surface, not as footnotes (`assessment/harness/probes/g1_declared.py`); unchanged. **G1-O (observed)** — the family preservation rate (the L3+ share of scored qualifier families, D9) when the pinned consumer restates that same captured surface at indirect compressi

air:revision-semantic.scope_note: Indicator G2 of the AI-ready data framework. Revision status machine-readable per value (preliminary/revised/final/benchmark), with scheduled-revision dates; EVAL: vintage disambiguation (ties C3)

air:classification-vintage-identity.scope_note: Indicator G3 of the AI-ready data framework. Stable series IDs; machine-readable crosswalks when classifications or geographies change (industry codes, boundary revisions)

air:authority-metadata.scope_note: Indicator G4 of the AI-ready data framework. Issuing authority, statutory mandate, and statistical-vs-administrative provenance carried as structured metadata — the trust signal AI rankers need to prefer authoritative sources over aggregators

air:disclosure-semantic.scope_note: Indicator G5 of the AI-ready data framework. Suppression and disclosure-avoidance documented machine-readably with unique identifiers (strengthens the guide's own bullet from prose to spec)

air:measurement-protocol-provenance.scope_note: Indicator G6 of the AI-ready data framework. Collection instrument/protocol carried as a versioned epoch on the series; changes annotated machine-readably with reason and inter-epoch crosswalk (SDMX break-in-series class metadata). The consumer-side test: an AI system asked to compare values across a break must surface the break

air:discovery.scope_note: Whether a machine can find that a data product exists at all. Indicator group A. Protocol §7 names the dimension spelled out and refuses `D1`-`D4` because the letter D is already load-bearing twice.

air:retrieval.scope_note: Whether a machine that knows a product exists can obtain it. Indicator group A.

air:interpretability.scope_note: Whether a machine that has the bytes can tell what they mean. Indicator groups B and G.

air:trust.scope_note: Whether a machine can tell where the product came from and under what terms it may be used. Indicator groups D and F.

air:robot-txt.scope_note: The Robots Exclusion Protocol: a site-root file declaring which paths a named user-agent may fetch. Standardised as RFC 9309 (2022); the declared layer of indicator A4/A11.

air:sitemap.scope_note: An XML file enumerating a site's URLs for crawlers, with optional change frequency and last-modified hints. Indicator A5.

air:well-known-uris.scope_note: RFC 8615: the `/.well-known/` path prefix reserving a site-root namespace for machine-discoverable metadata files.

air:schema-org-dataset.scope_note: The schema.org vocabulary type for a dataset, embedded as JSON-LD or microdata on a product page so a crawler can parse it. Indicator A6.

air:dcat.scope_note: W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary: an RDF vocabulary for describing catalogs of datasets and their distributions. Indicator A6.

air:data-json.scope_note: The Project Open Data catalog file a US federal agency publishes at `/data.json`, enumerating its public data assets. Indicator D4.

air:content-negotiation.scope_note: HTTP `Accept`-header negotiation, by which one URL serves a human page or a machine representation depending on what the client asks for.

air:persistent-identifier.scope_note: A durable, resolvable identifier for a product or vintage (DOI, ARK, w3id) that survives site reorganisation. Indicator A7.

air:croissant.scope_note: MLCommons' JSON-LD metadata format for machine-learning datasets, layered on schema.org. Indicator A6.

air:model-context-protocol.scope_note: An open protocol by which a model client discovers and calls tools and data sources at inference time. FRONTIER CANDIDATE, as_of 2026-01: postdates the policy corpus, so protocol §4 reports it on the frontier track and never in the core score.

air:llm-txt.scope_note: A proposed site-root markdown file offering an LLM-oriented map of a site's content. FRONTIER CANDIDATE, as_of 2026-01; the proposal is open for community input and is not an established practice.

air:sdmx.scope_note: Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange: the ISO 17369 standard for exchanging statistical data and its structural metadata, including break-in-series class metadata. Indicator G6.

air:search-engine-optimization.scope_note: Optimising a page to RANK in a search engine's list of links, where the user then clicks through. First documented use attributed to John Audette (Multimedia Marketing Group), 1997; the attribution is contested — Bruce Clay, Bob Heyman and Leland Harden are all credited around the same date. Optimises for: position in a ranked list of destinations.

air:answer-engine-optimization.scope_note: Optimising content to be the SOURCE a direct-answer engine cites when it returns one answer rather than a list. Industry origin, no academic paper; in circulation by 2023-05. Optimises for: being the cited source of a single returned answer (Google AI Overviews, Perplexity).

air:generative-engine-optimization.scope_note: Optimising content for visibility inside a response a generative engine COMPOSES from many sources. The only member of this lineage with an academic origin: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit, Kalyan, Narasimhan and Deshpande, arXiv:2311.09735 (2023-11-16), published at KDD 2024. It models a generative engine as retrieval plus synthesis and proposes metrics for citations dispersed through a composed text. Optimises for: share of a synthesised answer, not position in a list.

air:ai-optimization.scope_note: AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION — recorded with its ambiguity rather than resolved. At least three live senses in trade use: (a) making a brand or content absorbable by an LLM; (b) optimising specifically for Google AI Overviews, launched 2024-05-14, sometimes written `AI Overview Optimization`; (c) using AI inside one's own SEO workflow. Industry origin, 2024-2025, no consensus definition in the literature as of 2026. Optimises for: whichever of the three the writer meant, which is why an assessment must say which.
